bib.title: Large Language Models are Effective Text Rankers with Pairwise Ranking Prompting

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Large Language Models are Effective Text Rankers with Pairwise Ranking Prompting", Zhen Qin, Rolf Jagerman, Kai Hui, Honglei Zhuang, Junru Wu, Le Yan, Jiaming Shen, Tianqi Liu, Jialu Liu, Donald Metzler, Xuanhui Wang, Michael Bendersky (Google Research). The PDF is arXiv:2306.17563v2 [cs.IR], dated 28 Mar 2024. The extraction names no venue, so I record it as a preprint. The filename says 2023 (the v1 date). I did not confirm a published venue from the text.

COVERAGE: 58,319 of 58,319 chars read. That covers the main text, Tables 1-8, the limitations, appendices A-E and the references (skimmed). No extraction faults. The figures are only partly visible as text (Figures 1-3). I did not run the figure script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Pairwise Ranking Prompting (PRP) with a 20B open model matches or beats much larger blackbox LLM rerankers and is competitive with supervised rerankers on TREC-DL.
  number: FLAN-UL2 20B PRP-Sliding-10 reaches NDCG@1 78.29 / NDCG@10 72.65 on DL2019 and 85.80 / 70.46 on DL2020. RankGPT gpt-4 reaches 82.56 / 75.59 on DL2019 and 78.40 / 70.56 on DL2020. monoT5 3B (supervised) reaches 71.83 NDCG@10 on DL2019.
  setup: Rerank the BM25 top 100 passages for each query. TREC-DL2019 has 43 queries and DL2020 has 54, both on the MS MARCO v1 corpus of 8.8M passages. All PRP runs are unsupervised, with no fine-tuning.
  quote: "PRP variants based on FLAN-UL2 with 20B parameters can achieve best results on all metrics on TREC-DL2020, and are only second to the blackbox, commercial gpt-4 based solution on NDCG@5 and NDCG@10 on TREC-DL2019, which has an estimated 50X larger model size."
  where: Section 4.3 and Table 2, about chars 17-21k
- claim: PRP beats the other unsupervised LLM rerankers by a wide margin. The comparison is made on the same models, so it is fair.
  number: Over 10% on all metrics against RankGPT with text-davinci-003 (175B). On FLAN-UL2 20B, DL2020 NDCG@10 is 70.68 for PRP-Allpair against 65.39 for relevance generation (RG) and 60.02 for UPR.
  setup: Same as the claim above.
  quote: "Our best methods out-perform RankGPT based on text-davinci-003 with 175B parameters by over 10% on all ranking metrics, and are competitive to supervised methods on all ranking metrics."
  where: Section 4.3
- claim: One prompt template works across seven BEIR datasets. PRP-Sliding-10 on FLAN-UL2 slightly beats the supervised RankT5 on average.
  number: Average NDCG@10 is 53.55 for PRP-Sliding-10 FLAN-UL2, 53.34 for RankT5 3B, 51.33 for RankGPT gpt-3.5-turbo and 45.23 for BM25. PRP-Sliding-10 beats RankT5 on 5 of 7 datasets and beats RankGPT on all 7.
  setup: BEIR Covid, Touche, DBPedia, SciFact, Signal, News and Robust04, reranking BM25 top 100. The same prompt template is used for all datasets.
  quote: "PRP-Sliding-10 with FLAN-UL2 can slightly outperform the state-of-the-art RankT5 ranker on average, and outperform RankT5 on 5 out of 7 datasets."
  where: Section 5.3 and Table 3
- claim: Listwise prompting is fragile and sensitive to input order. PRP is far more robust.
  number: RankGPT gpt-3.5-turbo falls from NDCG@10 65.80 to 32.77 when the BM25 order is inverted. PRP-Allpair falls from 72.42 to 72.40.
  setup: TREC-DL2019. The pair order is swapped and the LLM is queried twice per pair as a debiasing step.
  quote: "PRP-Allpair FLAN-UL2-20B Inverse BM25 74.42 74.48 72.40"
  where: Table 4
- claim: Listwise prompts on a moderate open model produced almost no usable output.
  number: none
  setup: The Sun et al. (2023b) listwise prompt run on FLAN-UL2 20B. The failure patterns they list are missing, rejection, repetition and inconsistency.
  quote: "we tried the same prompt from (Sun et al., 2023b) on the FLAN-UL2 model with 20B parameters, and found very few of the outputs to be usable."
  where: Section 2.2
- claim: Pointwise rerankers need calibrated probabilities and a scoring API, and listwise rerankers work only through a generation API. PRP supports both.
  number: Table 1 call counts are O(N) pointwise, O(N) listwise, and O(N²), O(N log N) or O(N) pairwise.
  setup: N is the number of documents ranked per query.
  quote: "Pairwise O(N 2), O(N log N ), O(N ) Yes Yes No"
  where: Table 1
- claim: Generation mode and scoring mode give nearly identical results, and malformed outputs are rare.
  number: About 0.02% of predictions do not follow the format. On FLAN-UL2 DL2019, NDCG@10 is 72.42 in scoring mode and 72.37 in generation mode.
  setup: PRP-Allpair on FLAN-T5-XL, FLAN-T5-XXL and FLAN-UL2.
  quote: "We found that there are only about 0.02% predictions that do not follow the format, which is neglectable and in stark contrast to the the listwise approaches."
  where: Section 6 and Table 5
- claim: Sliding window behaves like bubble sort. One backward pass fixes NDCG@1 and more passes improve the deeper metrics. A forward pass is poor.
  number: FLAN-UL2 on DL2019, NDCG@10 is 57.58 after 1 backward pass, 64.60 after 3 and 72.65 after 10. One forward pass gives 54.10.
  setup: TREC-DL2019, FLAN-UL2 20B. DL2020 shows the same pattern (Table 7).
  quote: "Strong NDCG@1 can already be achieved with one backward pass. As we conduct more passes, other Top-K ranking metrics get better."
  where: Appendix A, Tables 6-7
- claim: The efficiency trade-off between variants.
  number: PRP-Allpair makes O(N²) calls and is order-insensitive. PRP-Sorting uses heapsort at O(N log N). PRP-Sliding-K makes K passes at O(N) each.
  setup: Allpair gives each document 1 point per win and 0.5 per tie, and ties fall back to the initial (BM25) ranking.
  quote: "The clear drawback is its costly O(N 2) calls to LLM APIs, where N is the number of documents to be ranked for each query."
  where: Section 3.2-3.4
- claim: PRP on a commercial model improves further.
  number: PRP-Allpair with text-bison reaches NDCG@10 73.81 on DL19 and 71.66 on DL20.
  setup: Google text-bison, said to be comparable to gpt-3.5-turbo.
  quote: "PRP-Allpair text-bison 73.81 71.66"
  where: Appendix B, Table 8
- claim: Smaller PRP models still work.
  number: FLAN-T5-XL 3B PRP-Allpair reaches 69.75 NDCG@10 on DL2019.
  setup: Same TREC-DL setup.
  quote: "Results on FLAN-T5-XL and FLAN-T5-XXL are also competitive, showing that PRP generalizes to smaller LLMs due to the significant simplicity of the pairwise ranking comparisons."
  where: Section 4.3

LIMITS
- GPT models were not tested by the authors. GPT numbers come from other papers.
- The ranking methods are empirical. Pairwise comparisons are not guaranteed to be transitive, and noisy-sorting theory is left for future work.
- Only relevance-style ranking was tested. Non-standard tasks such as ArguAna counter-arguments are untested.
- Data leakage is not ruled out. FLAN has an MS MARCO QA task. The authors avoid the word "zero-shot".
- Efficiency is the open cost. Allpair is O(N²). Sliding-K depends on input order, and the paper shows "surprisingly good results" only for K=10.
- Every experiment reranks BM25 top 100, not a dense or hybrid first stage. There is no latency or cost measurement in the text.
- Dated: the models are FLAN-T5/UL2 and the baselines are 2023 GPT-3.5/GPT-4. The authors leave stronger LLMs such as GPT-4 as future work.
- Distilling LLM rankers into servable models is named as future work.
- The GPT-4 figure 75.59/70.56 is RankGPT's, from Sun et al. 2023b. Sun et al.'s GPT-4 variant that reranked gpt-3.5-turbo output was excluded from BEIR as an ensemble.

BUILDS ON
- Pointwise: relevance generation (Liang et al., 2022) and query generation (Sachan et al., 2022; Drozdov et al., 2023).
- Listwise: Sun et al. (2023b), RankGPT, and Ma et al. (2023), LRL.
- Supervised baselines: monoBERT (Nogueira and Cho, 2019), monoT5 (Nogueira et al., 2020), RankT5 (Zhuang et al., 2023), TART (Asai et al., 2023).
- Benchmarks and tools: BM25 via Pyserini (Lin et al., 2021), BEIR (Thakur et al., 2021), FLAN (Wei et al., 2021; Chung et al., 2022), UL2 (Tay et al., 2022a).
- Related work names HyDE (Gao et al., 2022) as an auxiliary use of LLMs, not a direct ranker.
- Sorting and win-ratio theory: Shah and Wainwright (2018). The authors call pairwise comparison a classic idea.

CODE: only the prompt template (Appendix E.1, and Figure 2).
Given a query {query}, which of the following two passages is more relevant to the query?
Passage A: {document1}
Passage B: {document2}
Output Passage A or Passage B:
Scoring (Eq. 2): s_i = 1·Σ_{j≠i} I[d_i>d_j] + 0.5·Σ_{j≠i} I[d_i=d_j]. A pair counts as a win only if both order-swapped prompts agree.

FIGURES
- Figure 1: pointwise relevance generation versus listwise permutation prompts. It shows what PRP replaces.
- Figure 2: the pairwise prompt, with generation mode ("Passage A") and scoring mode (log-likelihoods -0.0012 and -6.9116). Page 3. It is the clearest single picture of the method.
- Figure 3: one backward sliding-window pass (bubble-sort style). Page 4.
- I did not run the caption script. These are taken from the extracted text.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- The extraction does not state a publication venue.
- The paper does not mention chunking, query parsing, cross-encoder latency or cost. It supports only the reranking section.
- The target note's sources list does not include arXiv:2306.17563. The note's reranking table row "LLM pointwise, pairwise or listwise" (Raieli & Iuculano) is where this paper would be cited. The paper supports that row's "best quality, highest cost" only partly, because it shows no cost numbers and it shows PRP-Sliding reduces calls.
- The note's claim that LLM scoring is "never first stage" is not tested here. The paper covers reranking only.
- I read the target note (/Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/notes/05-chunking-query-parsing-and-reranking.md) and did not edit anything.
